$comment: THE PROOF KIT'S RELEASE ASSET, declared (Phase 536). The kit is distributed as ONE versioned archive, `proofs-kit-<version>.tar`, which the publish workflow builds and attaches to the `v<version>` release, and which an adopter pins by sha256 in its own `proofs/proofs-kit.json` exactly as every leg pins the prover in `fstar-pin.json`. This file is the archive's contents: `build-kit-asset.ps1` beside it reads `files` and nothing else, in the order it sorts them, so what the asset carries is decided here and nowhere else. Each entry is a file under `proofs/` (`path`) and where it sits in the archive (`as`). The archive is an uncompressed ustar tar with every entry's time at the Unix epoch, its mode 0644, its owner 0:0 and no owner names, its text LF, and its entries in ordinal order of `as` — so its sha256 is a function of these files' bytes alone, and `copies.json`'s `proofsKit.sha256` is the one this tree builds (the `Proofs.Kit` family holds it). Roles: `engine` and `support` are the scripts (an adopter edits none of them); `template` files are copied once and edited by the adopter, so a template moving reaches an adopter as a release note, never as a stale copy; `pin` is the prover declaration the engine reads; `floor` is the hand-written runtime the extracted F# compiles against, which an adopter COMMITS in its own oracle directory (its oracle project may compile nothing outside it) and the engine holds to this asset's bytes (`-FloorDir`); `model` files are checked READ-ONLY from the asset (`-ModelDirs`): an adopter opens them, never copies them, and never declares one. `models` is every module an adopter may open: the two shared modules every model opens, the generic theorems, and the reference instance on the skeleton tree. `Vocabulary.fst` and `WireVersioning.fst` are not here: one is generated from this repository's IDL, the other is a theorem about that IDL's diff.

files.note: How a repository adopts the kit.
The claims-ladder schema, read in place.
This declaration, so an adopter can read what each file is for.
The builder, so the asset says how it was made.
The engine. An adopter's `proofs/check.ps1` calls it from the materialised asset.
The engine's refusals held to their exit codes; an adopter's caller runs it after a green leg.
Dot-sourced by the engine from its own directory; not optional.
The post-pass's go-red proof and its retirement condition.
The relocation-halt measurement over recorded ledgers.
Its tests.
The caller: resolves the pinned asset, then runs the engine from it.
The CI job; its cache key hashes the kit pin.
The roster and budget declaration.
The claims ladder.
The never-packed oracle project.
The instantiation template: `Skeleton.fst` with holes, instantiated and never edited.
The post-pass's fixture; never registered in a roster.
The pinned prover: the kit version determines it.
The runtime floor; grows as models reach further into F*'s library.
The second half of the floor.
